description: S47 T7 (TC9/OL3): tools.mine.list is the CALLER's own inventory — there is no `agent` param to name a subject, because the subject is the identity stamped on the step, and this is what an agent of that stamp sees. Two rows, and the two rows are the whole point: `read` comes from the code with `granted_by:["default"]` (the unconditional grant put it there, and the engine's allow sentence travels verbatim), and `acme.search` is a qualified MCP name that exists in this answer ONLY because this agent declares it — a peer's private server is not filtered out here, it was never in the input, which is how MC2 is structural rather than a filter (no field of this result can name another agent's world, not even a count). No row says `not_granted`: a tool the agent was not given is ABSENT, never listed as refused, so the list is an inventory and not a survey of what was withheld. `held` restates the count so a badge cannot disagree with the array.

tool.name: read
tool.description: Read a file from the workspace, returning its contents with line numbers.

path.description: path relative to the step's working directory
